transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

No, the motor is not likely on its way out. The V15 Detect uses a laser to count dust and an auto-mode that adjusts suction based on what it finds. When you move from tiles (low debris) to a rug (higher debris load), the vacuum automatically ramps up power to clean effectively; this causes the noise to rise and the battery to drain faster for those few seconds. The screen fluctuating is likely the sensor recalibrating or the mode adjusting. To confirm this is normal behaviour, does the suction visibly increase on the display when you hit the rug, then settle once it has cleaned a section?

I'm not sure the screen shows suction as such. What I can see is the runtime number jumping up and down and the particle bar chart changing while I clean, and the screen says 'Auto' in the middle. There are no warning symbols or red lights, and no burning smell, heat or sparks, so nothing looks dangerous. It's just the noise change that worries me.

That suggests it is working as designed. The 'Auto' mode uses the laser sensor to detect dust; when you hit the rug, the vacuum detects more debris (shown by the particle bar rising) and automatically increases suction power to clean effectively. This increased load makes the motor louder and drains the battery faster for those moments, while the runtime number fluctuates because it is recalculating based on that higher power draw. Since there are no error codes, burning smells, or warning lights, this is normal behaviour and not a sign of a failing motor. You do not need to report it as faulty; you can continue using it safely.

candidates: Laser dust sensor reacting to rug texture (normal behaviour) (high)
Auto mode adjusting suction based on debris load (medium)
